classification: conditional law with distinguishing finite vectors; Shannon argument cited, not Lean-formalized
statement: For finite n>=2, uniform truth X, an n-ary symmetric channel X->Z with error c in [0,1], and X->Z->Y^K->A, I(X;A)<=I(X;Z)=log2(n)-h2(c)-c*log2(n-1).
conditions: The reports have a joint kernel conditional on Z alone; pairwise conditional independence is neither required for this bound nor a substitute for the Markov condition.

Aggregation uses reports alone, or randomness conditionally independent of X given the reports. A revealed channel-error/cause indicator, side channel or truth probe is extra input and must be included before applying DPI.
c is the declared crossover probability of this symmetric channel; neither unanimity nor a shared-cause frequency identifies it without a model.
No private p, hypothesis of M/3, or governance model M/4 is changed. The old always-wrong active cause with private p>0 is a different joint law.
Both c=0 and c=1 are permitted. c=(n-1)/n gives zero information; for binary c=1 the channel is an invertible complement and gives one bit. This quantity is not monotone over all c in [0,1].

proofChain.argument: Uniform X and the symmetric kernel imply uniform Z. The posterior of X given Z has masses 1-c and c/(n-1) on the other symbols, so H(X|Z)=h2(c)+c*log2(n-1), with 0 log 0=0.

The declared Markov kernels imply I(X;Y^K|Z)=0 and I(X;A|Y^K)=0. The chain rule and nonnegative conditional mutual information give I(X;A)<=I(X;Y^K)<=I(X;Z). No independence among reports given Z is needed for this inequality.

Published capacityP0 computes this expression as mutual information for single-dominant-factor@1 at private p=0, for every positive K. In that instance all reports are copies of Z, so equality is already exact; a finite-copy vector is not a new discovery.

Compose the symmetric lineage channel with the published decisionInformation table for c=0, p=e and plurality-uniform-ties@1. Exact rational joint tables give a finite sequence of gaps to capacityP0. Under the separately declared fixed-parameter iid recovery hypothesis, consistency and finite-alphabet entropy continuity imply the limit; the finite sequence does not prove the limit.

fanoBoundary.known: Fano gives H(X|Z)<=h2(P[X!=Z])+P[X!=Z]*log2(n-1). For uniform X this is a lower bound on I(X;Z), not the proposed upper bound.
fanoBoundary.equalityCondition: The symmetric channel supplies equality in the entropy expression. A marginal error probability alone does not.
fanoBoundary.negative: A binary uniform source with P(Z=1|X=0)=0 and P(Z=0|X=1)=1/2 has error 1/4 and I=0.311278124459..., larger than 1-h2(1/4)=0.188721875540....

relationToF1.object: F1 concerns deterministic partitions U,V of one uniformly weighted N-element universe, in the maintained refinement order.
relationToF1.quantity: RI_H=H(U)+H(V)-H(join)-H(meet)=I(U;V)-H(G)=I(U;V|G), where join is the common refinement (U,V) and G is their common coarsening, a deterministic function of each.
relationToF1.bound: RI_H<=log2(N)-2+2/N; N=1,2 have zero maximum. This is not I(truth;aggregate); N need not equal the truth alphabet n.
relationToF1.jointUse: Apply F1 only when the partition/uniform-universe hypotheses hold. Apply the lineage ceiling only to a designated X and its declared Markov channel. If both models are supplied, both bounds may be written beside their own quantities; taking their minimum as a bound on either quantity is invalid.
separators: Uniform binary truth with noiseless Z has I(X;Z)=1 while F1 on N=2 has maximum RI_H=0.

Let X,Z be independent uniform bits (c=1/2), and R independent uniform on four symbols. The path partitions of R have RI_H=1/2. Reports can ignore Z and output those two views of R, so X->Z->reports holds and I(X;reports)=0. On the full uniform 16-atom (X,Z,R) universe F1 still applies (c_16=2.125), but RI_H=1/2 exceeds the zero lineage ceiling.
relationToF1.notAdded: No proof of F1 is redone; its existing path witness and public c_n are reused.

literature.addsHere: Explicit lineage-channel conditions, reuse of the already published expression, and vectors separating truth information from partition residual. No new information-theory inequality or inference without truth is claimed.

evidenceLimits: No general Lean proof of Shannon DPI here.
